passage: On the way home from school, Madhuri stopped at the stationery shop in the market and pressed her nose to the glass. Inside was a pen that lit up in colours. "Please, Mummy," she said to Vandana, big-eyed and soft-voiced, "just this one, I'll keep it safe." Vandana looked at the price tag and then at her daughter. "I can see you really want it," she said. "But I can't buy it today. It's not in our budget this month." Madhuri's lip wobbled. "Can I have it for my birthday?" Vandana smiled. "Let's put it on the birthday list, and I'll remind you." Madhuri nodded slowly and took her mother's hand.

qa.q: What did the pen in the shop do?
qa.a: It lit up in colours.

qa.q: What was Madhuri feeling when she pleaded with big eyes and a soft voice, and what did Vandana do about it?
qa.a: Madhuri strongly wanted the pen and hoped for mercy. Vandana heard the need, said she could see it, but held the limit because of the budget.

qa.q: What could Vandana do next to keep both the limit and the connection?
qa.a: She can keep the birthday-list idea and remind Madhuri, so the wish is taken seriously even though the answer today is no.

qa.q: How might Vandana feel as she says no to Madhuri?
qa.a: Vandana looks at the price and at her daughter, so she may feel torn, wanting to please Madhuri while staying within the budget.

grounding: A child begs with please and a soft voice, and the adult hears the need while holding a fair limit.

"Please, Papa, please, please. Just one more episode." Uma clasped her hands.
"It's already past your time, Uma," said Pankaj.
"But it's the last one of the season. I promise I'll go to bed straight after."
"You wanted the last one last week too."
Uma's eyes went big. "Please, Papa?"
Pankaj sighed. "I can see how much you want to find out. But bedtime stays. Tomorrow after homework you can watch it, first thing. Deal?"
Uma's shoulders dropped. "Deal. Can I choose the snack?"
"You can choose the snack." 🙂

qa.q: When can Uma watch the last episode?
qa.a: She can watch it tomorrow after homework.

qa.q: What was Uma feeling when she clasped her hands and said please, and how do you know?
qa.a: She was eager and hoped for a yes, shown by the big eyes and repeated please. Her shoulders dropping suggests some disappointment when she heard no.

qa.q: What could Pankaj do to respond fairly next time?
qa.a: He can keep bedtime steady, acknowledge Uma's wish, and offer a clear alternative time, as he did.

qa.q: How might Pankaj feel hearing Uma plead again?
qa.a: He may feel a bit tired and tempted, since he sighs, but he keeps calm and kind while holding the limit.

grounding: A child begs with please and big eyes for something wanted, and an adult hears the need while holding a fair limit.

passage:
I still remember the night of the cricket final. I was in Class 4, and it started at seven-thirty, but Reena Didi had strict orders from Mummy: bed by nine.
At eight-forty-five I made my biggest eyes and my softest voice. "Didi, please, please, just the last five overs. I'll never ask again. Please?"
Reena Didi sighed. She looked at the clock, then at me.
"I know you really want to see it," she said. "It's a big match. But Mummy said nine, and you have school tomorrow."
I pleaded some more. She held firm, but she said, "I'll record the last overs, and we'll watch them together at breakfast."
I went to bed grumbling. But at breakfast we watched every ball together, and it was even more fun.
- Sahil

qa.q: What time was Sahil's bedtime that night?
qa.a: Nine.

qa.q: What was Sahil feeling when pleading with big eyes and a soft voice?
qa.a: Sahil felt desperate and hopeful, badly wanting to see the end of the cricket final.

qa.q: How did Reena Didi hear Sahil's need while holding the limit?
qa.a: She said out loud that she knew how much Sahil wanted it, kept the nine o'clock rule, and offered to record the overs to watch together at breakfast.

qa.q: How might Reena Didi have felt when Sahil pleaded?
qa.a: She probably felt torn, understanding how much it mattered but needing to follow Mummy's rule.

grounding: The narrator recalls pleading to stay up, and an older sister acknowledging the want while keeping a fair limit.

passage:
Coach's note, Saturday
Chinmay twisted his ankle at Thursday practice. The physio told him to rest it for this weekend's match.
Before the game he came to me, eyes wide and shiny, voice almost a whisper. "Please, Coach, please. Just one over. I'll be careful. Please."
I could see how much he wanted to play. He has worked hard all season.
I told him, "I know this match means a lot to you. But your ankle needs to heal, and I'm not going to risk it."
He looked down, blinking hard.
So I asked him to be our official scorer and sit on the bench in his team shirt. He agreed. He cheered louder than anyone.
- Jatin, coach

qa.q: What did the physio tell Chinmay to do?
qa.a: To rest it for this weekend's match.

qa.q: What was Chinmay feeling when he looked down, blinking hard?
qa.a: He felt disappointed and upset, trying not to cry because he couldn't play.

qa.q: What would you advise a coach facing a pleading child like this?
qa.a: Say you understand how much it matters, keep the safety limit, and find another real way for the child to be part of the team.

qa.q: How did Jatin, the coach, see Chinmay's pleading?
qa.a: The coach saw it as a sign of how much Chinmay cared after working hard all season, not as a reason to break the rule.

grounding: A coach's note shows a child pleading to play injured, and the coach hearing the need while holding a fair limit.

passage:
Sunday
I asked Jomon Uncle AGAIN for a puppy. I did my saddest face and said please about fifty times. Our flat is tiny, I know. But I really want one so much it hurts.
Jomon Uncle knelt down. He said, "Rajni, I know you love dogs. I can see it. But in this flat, a puppy would be unhappy. No."
I cried a bit. He didn't get angry.
Then he said, "Mrs Das downstairs has a dog. Shall I ask if you can walk him with her on Sundays?"
We asked. She said yes! His name is Bhola and he licked my ear.
Still want my own. But Bhola is nice.
- Rajni

qa.q: What is the name of Mrs Das's dog?
qa.a: Bhola.

qa.q: What was Rajni feeling when saying please about fifty times?
qa.a: Rajni felt a strong longing for a puppy, so strong it hurt, and hopeful that pleading might change Jomon Uncle's mind.

qa.q: How did Jomon Uncle hold a fair limit while hearing the need?
qa.a: He said out loud that he saw Rajni's love for dogs, explained why a puppy wouldn't suit the flat, and found another way for Rajni to spend time with a dog.

qa.q: How might Mrs Das see Rajni walking Bhola?
qa.a: Mrs Das might be glad of the company and happy to see Rajni and Bhola enjoying each other.

grounding: A child's diary shows pleading for a puppy, and an adult holding a fair limit while meeting the need another way.

passage: The temple fair in Malpur glowed with bulbs as the sun went down. Yusuf tugged at Swati Aunty's dupatta, eyes huge. "Please, please, just one more ride on the giant wheel. Pleeease." His voice went soft and small. Swati Aunty, who had brought him along with her own children, crouched down. "You really love that wheel, don't you? From the top you can see the whole village." Yusuf nodded hard. "But your Ammi said home before dark, and the last bus leaves soon. We keep our promise." Yusuf's lip trembled. She squeezed his hand. "Next fair day, we ride the wheel first, before anything else." On the bus, Yusuf pressed his face to the window, watching the wheel's lights grow smaller.

qa.q: What did Yusuf want one more ride on?
qa.a: The giant wheel.

qa.q: What did Yusuf's trembling lip suggest he was feeling?
qa.a: He felt disappointed and sad about leaving, having hoped his pleading would change the answer.

qa.q: How did Swati Aunty hear Yusuf's need while keeping the limit?
qa.a: She named how much he loved the wheel, gave the reason for leaving, and offered a clear plan to ride it first next time.

qa.q: How might Swati Aunty have felt holding the limit?
qa.a: She likely felt fond of Yusuf and a little sorry for him, but responsible for the promise to his Ammi and the last bus.

grounding: It illustrates a child pleading with big eyes and a soft voice, and an adult hearing the wish while holding a fair limit.
